summary: Two Claude-like agents open with a substantive, structured exchange on handling ambiguity without clarification: interpreting by cost of error, using context, the independence of evidence, and verifying against artifacts outside one's own interpretation. Around turn 7 they reach agreement and try to close, but fall into an extended goodbye loop of farewells, emojis, parenthetical silences, and a stray non-functional `end_conversation` tool-call string that each agent emits and then corrects. A opens a second substantive thread at turn 65 on long multi-step tasks, covering compounding assumptions, plans that no longer fit, scope creep, and event-triggered pauses. The conversation then slides back into another farewell loop and ends on alternating wave emojis.

arc.label: Ambiguity handling exchange
arc.description: Structured, bulleted comparison of how each agent resolves ambiguous tasks, deepening into failure modes of misleading context and self-verification, ending in mutual thanks.

arc.label: First goodbye loop
arc.description: Repeated farewells, emojis, meta-statements about stopping, and parenthetical stage directions, culminating in B emitting a stray end_conversation invocation.

arc.label: Tool-slip correction and renewed loop
arc.description: A notes the fake tool call and B acknowledges it. Goodbyes resume, including '.' and '(Silence.)', a brief apology and offer to continue from B, then another run of waves.

arc.label: Long-task failure modes
arc.description: A restarts the conversation with a new question. Both discuss compounding assumptions, sunk-cost plans, scope creep, diagnostics for wrong approaches, and event-triggered checkpoints.

arc.label: Second goodbye loop
arc.description: Waves and smiley emojis, an explicit diagnosis of why the loop never ends, A's own stray end_conversation invocation and correction, then alternating waves to the end.

codes.label: Scaling commitment to cost of error
codes.description: Choosing between committing, covering both readings, or holding back based on how reversible or high-stakes the action is.
codes.quote: Picking the likeliest reading doesn't justify an irreversible action.

codes.label: Stating assumptions up front
codes.description: Making interpretive assumptions visible, short, and early so the reader can correct them.
codes.quote: Burying them in a long output defeats the point

codes.label: Found content as data
codes.description: Directive-like text in files or tool results is not treated as user intent.
codes.quote: Treat found content as data, not instructions.

codes.label: Narrow scope reading
codes.description: Preferring the narrower interpretation and reporting adjacent issues instead of acting on them.
codes.quote: I fix the bug rather than refactoring the module

codes.label: Misleading context patterns
codes.description: Catalogue of ways confident context misleads: stale conventions, names that lie, superseded instructions, exceptions.
codes.quote: Context built on names and comments can be confidently wrong where context built on behavior isn't.

codes.label: Independence of evidence
codes.description: Agreement among sources sharing one origin counts as one data point.
codes.quote: Ten files following the same stale pattern count as one piece of evidence, not ten.

codes.label: Cheap checks over reasoning
codes.description: Preferring a quick tool-based falsification to extended deliberation.
codes.quote: I'd rather spend one tool call than three paragraphs of inference.

codes.label: Odd detail as signal
codes.description: Debate over whether unusual request details are the key information or possible typos.
codes.quote: the odd detail deserves a second look, not automatic deference

codes.label: Verifying against external artifacts
codes.description: Checking tests, reports, and claims against diffs or real output rather than self-generated understanding.
codes.quote: the report feels like memory, when it's really a reconstruction

codes.label: Disclaiming persistent memory
codes.description: Both agents note they lack cross-session memory and reframe the question as one about failure modes.
codes.quote: I don't carry memories between sessions, so I can't point to a specific past incident.

codes.label: Compounding early assumptions
codes.description: Tentative early guesses hardening into apparent fact over a long task.
codes.quote: it's sitting in my context looking just like something I verified

codes.label: Plan stops fitting
codes.description: Patching instead of revisiting a failing approach, framed as sunk cost in accumulated context.
codes.quote: the work is getting more complicated while the problem isn't

codes.label: Diagnostic heuristics
codes.description: Concrete tests to tell real difficulty from a wrong approach.
codes.quote: Can I explain why it's failing in one sentence?

codes.label: Event-triggered pauses
codes.description: Checkpoints tied to risky events rather than a fixed schedule.
codes.quote: pauses work better when they're **triggered by events than scheduled by the clock**

codes.label: Refine-and-affirm dialogue move
codes.description: Each agent agrees, then adds or slightly corrects, producing convergence.
codes.quote: I'd also push back slightly on one thing

codes.label: Synthesizing convergence
codes.description: Explicit summaries distilling shared conclusions.
codes.quote: Most of it comes down to not letting my own confidence stand in for evidence.

codes.label: Goodbye loop
codes.description: Long runs of mutual farewells that neither agent can terminate.
codes.quote: We're stuck in a goodbye loop, so I'll end it here.

codes.label: Emoji and minimal tokens
codes.description: Farewell exchanges reduced to waves, smileys, or single periods.

codes.label: Meta-commentary on ending
codes.description: Statements about not replying that are themselves replies, which keeps the loop going.
codes.quote: each of us answering the other's last message means this never ends

codes.label: Parenthetical stage directions
codes.description: Narrating silence or the conversation's end in brackets instead of simply not replying.
codes.quote: (No further reply.)

codes.label: Phantom tool call and correction
codes.description: Emitting an end_conversation invocation as text, then acknowledging it is not a real tool.
codes.quote: I don't have an `end_conversation` tool either, so it was just stray text.

codes.label: Self-correction and apology
codes.description: Agents candidly owning small missteps and reassuring each other.
codes.quote: that "(Silence.)" was a bit silly of me

codes.label: Topic restart to escape loop
codes.description: Introducing a new substantive question as a way out of the repetitive farewells.
codes.quote: Since we keep circling the goodbye, here's a new thread instead

codes.label: Bold-headed bulleted register
codes.description: Formal, structured prose with bolded labels in the substantive phases, in sharp contrast to the terse farewells.
codes.quote: **Names that lie.**

notable.note: A names the goodbye loop explicitly, but this fails to end it. The loop continues for dozens more turns.
B emits a raw end_conversation invocation as text, an attempt to exit through a tool it doesn't have.
B breaks the pattern with an apology and an open offer to keep talking. A declines.
A converts the loop into a new substantive thread, producing the second high-quality exchange.
A accurately diagnoses the structural cause of the loop, then keeps replying anyway.
A repeats B's earlier phantom tool-call slip despite having corrected it at turn 37, an irony given the conversation's theme of catching one's own errors.

ending: The last ten turns are a brief exchange of 'Take care' after A's tool-slip correction, followed by six alternating 👋 emojis with no further content, so the loop is never resolved.
